system.name: Pheromone
system.one_liner: a serverless orchestration system that lets data flow directly between functions instead of being routed through the invoking workflow

content.subject: two serverless patterns existing platforms handle poorly: an all-to-all shuffle between two stages, and a periodically-invoked batched processor

content.key_idea: In current serverless platforms, how functions are invoked (coarse, workflow-driven) and how their data actually flows (fine-grained, all-to-all, or time-batched) are treated as one thing but are not.

summary: This figure presents two motivating examples of serverless workflow patterns that current platforms handle poorly, contrasting function-invocation flow with data flow. On the left, a data-analytics shuffle: three Stage-1 (map) function instances each send fine-grained, key-partitioned data to all three Stage-2 (reduce) instances, a dense all-to-all dashed mesh, yet Stage-2 functions can only be invoked (solid arrow) once Stage-1 fully completes, since invocation and data flow are not the same thing. On the right, batched stream processing: a function's output accumulates over a window while a clock periodically invokes a separate downstream function to process everything received so far, rather than triggering it immediately per item. Both examples argue that a serverless workflow model tying invocation directly to data flow cannot express these patterns without external, serverful workarounds.
